subject: ela
intro: Multiple-choice quiz on using multimedia and visual displays in presentations: choosing the element that clarifies a point, judging whether media clarifies or distracts, and explaining how an element strengthens audience understanding.

items.prompt:
Maria gives a talk about hummingbirds. She wants the audience to hear exactly what a hummingbird's wings sound like in flight. Which presentation element is an audio component?
A) A recorded sound clip of the buzzing wings
B) A photograph of a hummingbird at a flower
C) A labeled diagram of a hummingbird's body
D) A map showing where hummingbirds live
items.answer: A) A recorded sound clip of the buzzing wings

steps: The question asks for an audio (sound) component. A recorded sound clip is something the audience hears, so A is the audio element.
B (photograph), C (diagram), and D (map) are all visual displays the audience sees, not audio, so they do not fit.
Because only one option is a sound the audience hears, A is the single best answer.

items.prompt:
During a presentation, Devon wants to show how a single butterfly looks up close so the audience can see the patterns on its wings. Which element would best show this?
A) A clear, close-up photograph of the butterfly
B) Background music playing during the talk
C) A sound effect of fluttering wings
D) A list of unrelated insect names
items.answer: A) A clear, close-up photograph of the butterfly

steps: To let the audience see the wing patterns, the audience needs to look at an image, so a close-up photograph (A) clarifies this point directly.
B (background music) and C (a sound effect) are audio and cannot show what the wings look like.
D is a list of names, which does not show the butterfly at all. Only A shows the visual detail, so it is correct.

items.prompt:
A presenter says, "I will use a visual display to organize my information." Which of these is a visual display?
A) A chart that organizes the data into rows and columns
B) A recorded voice reading the numbers aloud
C) A song played at the start of the talk
D) The sound of applause at the end
items.answer: A) A chart that organizes the data into rows and columns

steps: A visual display is something the audience sees, such as a chart, map, diagram, or slide. A chart (A) fits this category.
B is a recorded voice, C is a song, and D is a sound, so all three are audio elements, not visual displays.
Only A is a visual display, making it the single best answer.

items.prompt:
In her report, Jana explains how her town's population grew steadily from the year 2000 to the year 2020. She wants the audience to see the increase clearly across those twenty years. Which element would most clearly support this point?
A) A line graph showing population rising from 2000 to 2020
B) A single photograph of the town's main street
C) A cheerful song playing while she talks
D) A sound effect of a crowd cheering
items.answer: A) A line graph showing population rising from 2000 to 2020

steps: The point is how a quantity changed over time, and a line graph is built to show change across years, so A clarifies the information best.
B (a single photo) shows the town at one moment but not the growth over twenty years.

C (a song) and D (a cheering sound) add interest but show nothing about the numbers, reflecting the misconception that any added media improves a talk. A is correct because it matches the media type to data that changes over time.

items.prompt:
During a talk on rainforest animals, Carlos plays a recorded call of a howler monkey right after he describes how loud the monkeys are. The audience had never heard the call before. How does this sound clip clarify the information for the audience?
A) It lets the audience actually hear the loudness he described, making his point easier to understand
B) It makes the presentation more colorful to look at
C) It proves that Carlos owns expensive recording equipment
D) It replaces the need for Carlos to explain anything at all
items.answer: A) It lets the audience actually hear the loudness he described, making his point easier to understand

steps: Carlos's point is about how loud the monkeys are. Hearing the real call lets the audience experience that loudness directly, so the sound clarifies his spoken claim. A is correct.
B is wrong because a sound clip is heard, not seen, so it does not make the talk more colorful to look at.

C is off topic, since the equipment is not the point of the talk. D is wrong because the clip supports his explanation rather than replacing it. Only A connects the element to the specific information it clarifies.

items.prompt:
Priya is presenting about the parts of a volcano. She wants the audience to understand where the magma chamber, the vent, and the crater are located in relation to one another. She is deciding what to add to her slide. Which element would best clarify these locations?
A) A labeled diagram of a volcano with each part marked
B) A loud rumbling sound effect of an eruption
C) A bright, colorful image of a sunset over a mountain
D) Upbeat music to keep the audience's attention
items.answer: A) A labeled diagram of a volcano with each part marked

steps: The audience needs to see where each part sits in relation to the others, and a labeled diagram shows the layout with labels, so A clarifies the point.
B (a rumbling sound) is audio and cannot show where parts are located.

C is an attractive but unrelated image, and D is music for interest. Both reflect the misconception that decorative or entertaining media clarifies information when it does not. A is the single best answer.

items.prompt:
Ben is presenting survey results that compare how many students chose each of five after-school clubs. He reads the five numbers aloud one after another with no visual on the screen. By the third number, several listeners look confused and cannot remember the earlier totals. Ben has a slide ready and can add one element. Which choice would best clarify the comparison, and why?
A) A bar graph comparing the five clubs, because it lets the audience see all the totals side by side at once
B) A photo of the school building, because it makes the slide look more finished
C) Background music, because an exciting sound keeps the audience awake
D) Nothing extra, because spoken words alone are always enough for numbers
items.answer: A) A bar graph comparing the five clubs, because it lets the audience see all the totals side by side at once

steps: The problem is that listeners cannot hold five spoken numbers in mind to compare them. A bar graph shows all five totals together so the audience can see the comparison at a glance, so A both clarifies and explains why.
B adds a finished look but shows nothing about the totals, valuing decoration over clarity. C adds interest but does not help the audience compare numbers.

D reflects the misconception that visuals are never essential, but the confused listeners show the words alone were not enough. A is correct because it weighs clarity over decoration and solves the actual problem.

items.prompt:
Lena's slide about ocean pollution is packed with five flashing animations, three blinking arrows, a scrolling banner, and a paragraph of small text behind it all. As she speaks, the audience keeps watching the moving parts and loses track of her main idea: that plastic harms sea turtles. A classmate suggests a revision. Which revision would best clarify the information for the audience?
A) Remove the flashing animations and keep one clear image of a turtle with a short caption naming the main idea
B) Add even more animations so the slide is exciting enough to hold attention
C) Add background music so the audience has something to enjoy while reading
D) Leave the slide as it is, since a slide with many elements must be effective
items.answer: A) Remove the flashing animations and keep one clear image of a turtle with a short caption naming the main idea

steps: The slide's clutter hides the main idea, so the fix is to cut the distracting elements and keep one clear visual that supports the point. A removes the clutter and highlights the main idea, so it clarifies best.
B adds more animations, which would increase the distraction the audience already struggles with.

C adds music that does nothing to focus attention on the main idea. D reflects the misconception that more elements automatically make a slide effective, but the audience is clearly losing the point. A is the single best revision.
